svg.text: Total uncertainty in a final result, and the dimensions of physical quantities

g.text: 1 addition and subtraction: absolute uncertainties are added
2 multiplication and division: percentage uncertainties are added
R = 5.0 +/- 0.5 ohm (uncertainty to one significant figure)
3 power factor: percentage uncertainty x the power in the formula
Example 1.3 (cylinder): d = 1.25 cm, l = 3.35 cm, least count 0.01 cm; %d = 0.8%, %l = 0.3%;
Example 1.2: 3.25 kg + 0.01001 kg + 0.01002 kg = 3.27003 kg -> 3.27 kg (two decimal places)
five basic dimensions: length [L], mass [M], time [T], current [A], temperature [theta]
homogeneity: both sides of a correct equation have the same dimensions
S = v_i t + (1/2) a t^2, from rest: S = (1/2) a t^2
[S] = [a][t^2] -> [L] = [LT^-2][T^2] = [L] (1/2 has no dimensions)
derivation (Example 1.4): centripetal force depends on m, v and r
F = (constant) m^a v^b r^c ... (i)
F = (constant) m v^2 / r; the constant is 1 by experiment: F = m v^2 / r
limitations: the method cannot say where an equation is wrong, and a
dimensionally correct equation might still be wrong, because it gives no check
on numerical factors or constants: those come from experiment or a graph
quantities with the same dimension [L]: length, depth, height, diameter, light year

svg.text: Thumb rule for total uncertainty, and side-box facts carried in the text

g.text: addition and subtraction: absolute uncertainties are added. multiplication and division: percentage uncertainties are added.
power factor: power factor x percentage uncertainty. Example 1.1: V = 2.03 m x 1.22 m x 0.95 x 10^-2 m = 2.35277 x 10^-2 m^3 -> 2.4 x 10^-2 m^3 (0.95 has two figures)
travel time of light: Moon to Earth 1 min 20 s; Sun to Earth 8 min 20 s; Pluto to Earth 5 h 20 s. colour printing uses just cyan, magenta, yellow and black.
atomic clock: the caesium atomic frequency standard at NIST, Colorado, is the primary standard for the unit of time.
pendulum clock: the escapement (anchor, pallet, escape wheel) regulated by a pendulum made the pendulum clock practical.
beware: a calculator yields as many digits as its memory permits; round final answers to the correct number of significant figures.
mass as energy: E = mc^2; 1 kg of mass is equivalent to 9 x 10^16 J (Do You Know, 1.2).
